bib.title: AgentIR: Reasoning-Aware Retrieval for Deep Research Agents

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "AgentIR: Reasoning-Aware Retrieval for Deep Research Agents", Zijian Chen, Xueguang Ma, Shengyao Zhuang, Jimmy Lin, Akari Asai, Victor Zhong. arXiv:2603.04384v3, 9 Mar 2026. The header reads "Preprint. Work In Progress."

COVERAGE: 22 pages, all read. I read 68,171 chars in full, apart from the reference list (pp. 13-16), which I only skimmed for origins. That includes Appendices A-G, the prompts and the HyDE example. The note file was not read for claims. I only looked at its head, which describes a different ablation (a production support agent). The paper has no explicit limitations section.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Joint embedding of the agent's reasoning trace plus its query, with a retriever trained for it (AgentIR-4B), beats every baseline on end-to-end accuracy.
  number: 66.27% on Tongyi-DR (68.07% with the visit tool). Baselines: BM25 33.98, Qwen3-Embed-4B 48.67, Qwen3-Embed-8B 50.72, ReasonIR-8B 51.03.
  setup: BrowseComp-Plus; top-5 snippets of 512 tokens; LLM-judge accuracy. Agents were Tongyi-DR, gpt-oss-120B (high) and GLM-4.7. Single table, no seeds or confidence intervals reported.
  quote: "AgentIR-4B66.27 78.8625.91" (Table 1 row, columns Accuracy/Recall/Search Calls); "For Tongyi-DR, AgentIR-4B achieves 66.27% accuracy, a 17.60% absolute improvement over the Qwen3-Embed-4B backbone."
  where: Table 1, p.7; text p.8
- The same gain holds on the other agents with no retraining. The retriever was trained on rollouts from Tongyi-DR only.
  number: oss-120b-high 66.99 vs 47.59 (Qwen3-Embed-4B); GLM-4.7 64.66 vs 50.48.
  quote: "AgentIR-4B66.99 78.1324.08" and "AgentIR-4B64.66 79.2129.85"
  where: Table 1, p.7
- It beats a larger model and an expensive reranker.
  number: about 15 points over Qwen3-Embed-8B; about 10 points over listwise LLM reranking (55.66).
  setup: the reranker is Qwen3-8B listwise over the top-20 of Qwen3-Embed-4B.
  quote: "AgentIR-4B outperforms Qwen3-Embed-4B + LLM Rerank, a highly computationally expensive reranking method by approximately 10% absolute accuracy, despite performing no reranking."
  where: p.8
- Better retrieval means fewer agent search calls.
  number: 32.92 (BM25) to 25.91 (AgentIR-4B) on Tongyi-DR.
  quote: "the number of search calls decreases from 32.92 with BM25 to 25.91 with AgentIR-4B."
  where: p.8
- Recall of ground-truth evidence also rises.
  number: 78.86 vs 59.90.
  setup: Tongyi-DR, Table 1.
  quote: "Qwen3-Embed-4B 48.67 59.90 31.02"
  where: p.7
- Both components help independently, and combining them is best (ablation on the Qwen3-Embed-4B backbone).
  number: Tongyi-DR 48.67 (baseline), 55.54 (reasoning, no training), 59.40 (training, no reasoning), 66.27 (both).
  quote: "jointly embedding the agent reasoning without any fine-tuning improves accuracy from 48.67% to 55.54%. Training the retriever without using reasonings achieves 59.4%, and when combined with reasonings, accuracy further increases to 66.27%."
  where: Table 2, p.9; text p.8
- Caveat on the no-training result: on GLM-4.7, frozen reasoning-concat is flat.
  number: 50.90 vs 50.48.
  quote: "AgentIR-4B(w/o Training) 50.90 65.88 34.04"
  where: Table 2, p.9
- HyDE-style query expansion hurts in the agent setting, because it has no access to agent state.
  number: Reason-Rewriter + Reason-Embed-8B 31.08% on Tongyi-DR, against BM25 at 33.98.
  quote: "Without access to agent context, we found that their hypotheses often lead to misinterpretations and substantial hallucinations"
  where: Table 1, p.7; p.8; Fig 12, p.21. In the example the expander read "backroom studio" as a studio named "Backroom Studio" and invented "Los Angeles-based".
- Adding the global question Q (Agentic-R style) does not match the current reasoning.
  number: Tongyi-DR accuracy 63.25 with the same backbone and data; Agentic-R as released scored 44.70.
  quote: "Agentic-R 44.70 47.67 31.05"
  where: Tables 1 and 3, pp.7 and 10
- More history does not help, and including retrieved docs hurts.
  number: Tongyi-DR: current reasoning 66.27; prior queries 63.13; prior queries and reasonings 63.13; plus docs 60.00. For oss-120b the docs variant (58.67) falls below "None" (59.16).
  setup: each variant trained as a separate retriever from the same recipe. The docs variant is truncated to about 3 recent turns.
  quote: "Prior Queries & Reasonings & Docs 60.00 70.73 27.18"
  where: Table 3, p.10
- Noisy docs in the query cause retrieval failure spirals.
  number: 11.45% of runs had zero recall; those runs averaged 37.46 search turns vs 27.18 overall.
  setup: Tongyi-DR, docs variant.
  quote: "11.45% of the runs had zero recall, meaning no evident document is retrieved at any turn. These runs average 37.46 search turns, compared to 27.18 overall"
  where: p.10
- Extra prior reasoning turns do not improve accuracy. The current reasoning already covers most past clues, and older turns add wrong hypotheses.
  number: k=1 covers more than 40% of past clues.
  setup: Tongyi-DR; k in {1,2,5,9,17,all}; clues extracted by GLM-4.7.
  quote: "The current reasoning alone (k= 1) already covers more than 40% of all past clues."
  where: pp.11-12; Fig 3 and Fig 4(b). The numeric accuracy values are in the plot only.
- DR-Synth training data is small and cheap: 5,238 instances from 250 successful rollouts.
  number: 500 WebShaper (Q,A,P) triples, 250 answered correctly, 5,238 instances, corpus of 1,146,942 documents.
  quote: "After rollout generation on this corpus, 250 of the 500 WebShaper queries were correctly answered. Using these 250 correct trajectories, we obtain a total of 5,238 training instances"
  where: App. B, p.17
- Training recipe.
  number: lr 1e-4, batch 4, 2 epochs, LoRA, T=0.01, single H100. Labels from oracle listwise rerank of the top 50 plus gold P (reranker GLM-4.6); top-1 is the positive and the bottom 7 are hard negatives.
  quote: "We fine-tune with a learning rate of 1e-4, batch size 4, maximum document length 4096, and maximum query length 8192."
  where: App. B, p.17; Sec 3.3, pp.5-6
- Reasoning traces cost nothing extra, unlike HyDE or reranking.
  number: none
  quote: "HyDE that necessitates an additional, costly LLM call purely for query expansion, the Deep Research agent generates its reasoning trace entirely 'for free'"
  where: p.4

LIMITS
- One benchmark (BrowseComp-Plus, a fixed corpus), with no confidence intervals or seeds. Gaps of 1-3 points between the Table 3 variants are therefore weak evidence.
- Training and rollouts used one agent (Tongyi-DR) and one corpus built for WebShaper. Transfer was tested only on gpt-oss-120B and GLM-4.7.
- It needs agents that expose a reasoning trace, and it needs fine-tuning. The frozen "w/o Training" variant gives smaller gains and none on GLM-4.7.
- The abstract's "68%" is the Tongyi-DR+visit figure (68.07). Without visit it is 66.27.
- The abstract's "52%" for the baseline is Qwen3-Embed-8B with visit (51.93). The text says "approximately".
- The oracle reranker uses the gold answer, so it cannot be used outside training. The LLM-judged rerank baseline uses a small reranker, Qwen3-8B.
- Preprint, work in progress. The Agentic-R comparison is partly a different backbone and data, which the authors address with a replication. The paper has no explicit limitations section.
- The Prior Queries & Docs variant is truncated for context length, so it may be understated.

BUILDS ON: ReAct (Yao et al., 2023); HyDE (Gao et al., 2023); task-aware retrieval with instructions (Asai et al., 2023); Qwen3-Embedding (Zhang et al., 2025); BrowseComp-Plus (Chen et al., 2025b); WebShaper (Tao et al., 2025); Tongyi-DeepResearch; contrastive loss (Chen et al., 2020); listwise reranking (Sun et al., 2023; Ma et al., 2023); ReasonIR (Shao et al., 2025); RaDeR (Das et al., 2025); ReasonEmbed (Chen et al., 2025a); Agentic-R (Liu et al., 2026); conversational search with prior queries (Yu et al., 2021); LoRA (Hu et al., 2022); Tevatron (Ma et al., 2025). The authors also cite Lewis et al. 2020, Self-RAG (Asai et al., 2024) and Search-R1 (Jin et al., 2025).

CODE (verbatim, from Fig 5, App. A, p.17)
```
Instruction:
Given a user's reasoning followed by a web search query, retrieve relevant
passages that answer the query while incorporating the user's reasoning.
Query:
Reasoning:{reasoning}
Query:{query}
```
The duplicate "Query:" is intentional, to match Qwen3-Embedding's instruction format.

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p.1): AgentIR-4B vs Qwen3-Embedding-4B on the "backroom studio early 2010s euphoric" query. It shows the ambiguous query resolved by the reasoning trace.
- Fig 3 (p.11): (a) accuracy vs k history turns; (b) clue coverage by the k most recent reasonings. It shows diminishing returns.
- Fig 4 (p.11): (b) correct vs incorrect claims by k, showing noise growing with history.
- Fig 2: the oracle reranking pipeline for DR-Synth.
- Fig 12 (p.21): a HyDE-style hallucination example.

PROBLEMS: none. The extraction is clean, and the text contained no embedded instructions. The Fig 3 and Fig 4 data points are in plots only (not extracted).

Source file: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/generative-ai/02-rag-retrieval/sources/chen-2026-agentir.pdf

Relevance to note 11 (reported, not decided): the note's own ablation sits on a support bot with 44 tasks and does not cover agent-reasoning retrieval. This paper bears on its HyDE and query-expansion and tool-loop items. HyDE-style expanders without agent state performed worse than BM25 here. Conditioning on the agent's current reasoning gives a gain with no extra LLM call.
